text:
“Select service” is used somewhat loosely in Europe, but for a typical **120–250-key urban, airport or regional-city new build**, the following brands are commonly included in an initial operator/brand review.

### Core pan-European candidates

| Group | Brands commonly considered | Typical positioning |
|---|---|---|
| **IHG** | **Holiday Inn Express** | Economy/upper-economy; highly standardized, breakfast-led |
| **Hilton** | **Hampton by Hilton**, **Hilton Garden Inn** | Upper-economy to upper-midscale; Hampton is leaner, HGI generally has more F&B and meeting space |
| **Marriott** | **Moxy**, **Courtyard by Marriott**, **AC Hotels by Marriott**, **Four Points by Sheraton**, increasingly **Fairfield by Marriott** | Lifestyle select service through upper-midscale business-oriented products |
| **Accor** | **ibis budget**, **ibis**, **ibis Styles**, sometimes **TRIBE** | Economy through design-led midscale |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Place** | Upper-midscale select service, generally suited to larger urban and airport projects |
| **Radisson Hotel Group** | **Park Inn by Radisson**, **Prize by Radisson** | Upper-midscale and design-led economy |
| **Wyndham** | **Ramada by Wyndham**, **Wyndham Garden**, and—in appropriate markets—**Days Inn** or **Travelodge** | Economy through midscale; relevance varies significantly by country |

Holiday Inn Express remains particularly established, with more than 340 open and pipeline hotels in Europe as of June 2026. Hilton has similarly identified Hampton and Hilton Garden Inn as its principal European focused-service growth brands. Marriott formally groups Moxy, Courtyard, AC, Four Points and Fairfield within its select-service portfolio. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-adds-653-rooms-to-spanish-pipeline-with-a-trio-of-holiday-inn-express-signings?utm_source=openai))

### European operator-led alternatives

These are frequently considered alongside the global franchise systems, although the commercial structure may be a lease, management agreement, owner-operator arrangement or joint venture rather than a conventional franchise:

- **B&B HOTELS**
- **Motel One / The Cloud One**
- **Premier Inn**—especially in the UK, Ireland and Germany
- **Ruby Hotels**—now part of IHG
- **citizenM**—now within Marriott’s select portfolio
- **easyHotel**, primarily for highly price-sensitive, compact-room projects

B&B HOTELS describes itself as a leading and fast-growing European value hotel platform; Motel One explicitly targets new-build, mixed-use and conversion projects; and Premier Inn continues to seek new development sites in Germany as well as its core UK market. ([bbhotels-group.com](https://bbhotels-group.com/our-group/?utm_source=openai))

### If extended stay is part of the brief

Common select-service or limited-service extended-stay candidates include:

- **Residence Inn by Marriott** and **Element by Westin**
- **Staybridge Suites**
- **Home2 Suites by Hilton**
- **Hyatt House**
- **Aparthotels Adagio**

Home2 Suites is relatively new to Western Europe, while Residence Inn, Element, Staybridge Suites and Hyatt House have more established—but still market-selective—European development profiles. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/emea/releases/home2-suites-by-hilton-set-to-make-debut-in-western-europe?utm_source=openai))

### Practical first-round shortlist

For most European feasibility exercises, I would initially test:

1. **Holiday Inn Express**
2. **Hampton by Hilton**
3. **Moxy**
4. **Courtyard or Hilton Garden Inn**
5. **ibis Styles or ibis**
6. **B&B HOTELS**
7. **Motel One**
8. **Hyatt Place, AC Hotels or TRIBE** where the ADR and location support a more upscale/design-led product

The final shortlist should be narrowed by **country-level brand recognition, key count, room size, F&B requirement, labor model, loyalty contribution, territorial protection, fee structure and whether the operator will offer a lease, management agreement or franchise**. Brands such as **Garner, Spark by Hilton and Four Points Flex** may also appear in discussions, but they are generally more conversion-oriented than first-choice ground-up concepts.
